title: Extension by zero preserves stratified perfect local models
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$, and a uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ be a quasi-compact open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. For every subscheme $S$ below use its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], completed coefficient sheaf $A_S=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/\varpi^n)_S$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], and ordinary unbounded category $D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_S))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Identify restrictions of these coefficient sheaves by their canonical quotient-compatible inverse-image isomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]. Let $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_U))$. Suppose a finite stratification $U=\coprod_\alpha S_\alpha$ by locally closed subschemes [def-constructible-stratification] is given, with pro-etale covers on whose members $K|_{S_\alpha}$ is isomorphic to $A_{S_\alpha}\otimes_A^L P$ for a perfect $A$-complex $P$, meaning a bounded complex of finite projective $A$-modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex, def-weil-derived-tensor]. Use the exact module extension by zero $j_!$, applied termwise, on the localized ringed site [def-pur-localized-ringed-site, lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. Then the composites $S_\alpha\to U\to T$, together with any closed subscheme $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ whose underlying set is $T\setminus U$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], form a finite stratification of $T$. On each $S_\alpha$ the complex $j_!K$ has the original perfect models on the same covering members under the stated coefficient identifications, and $i^{-1}(j_!K)=0$, so the zero perfect complex is its model on $Z$.

source.place: Lemma 6.1.12 (j^*j_!\simeq\mathrm{id} and i^*j_!\simeq0 on unbounded derived categories, the source of the restriction identities), Proposition 6.6.11 (stratified perfect models) and Definition 6.7.6/Lemma 6.7.7 (compactification route). Extracted open-closed model argument, with Stacks Tags 09AA (lemma-closed-immersion), 09BN (lemma-open-immersion), 03DI (sites-modules-lemma-extension-by-zero), and 03DJ (sites-modules-lemma-extension-by-zero-exact).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] to the open immersion $j$. It identifies $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with $T_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$. Under this equivalence the completed coefficient sheaf restricts to $A_U$ by [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]. Thus [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] applies to the ring sheaf $A_T$ and gives exact module extension by zero. Applied degreewise, this functor preserves cohomology and hence quasi-isomorphisms: kernels and images are preserved by exactness. It therefore descends to the stated ordinary unbounded derived categories by their localization definition.

source.place: Tags 03DI/03DJ, lemma-extension-by-zero and lemma-extension-by-zero-exact; proetale.tex Definition 09AE, definition-extension-zero

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] to the commutative ring sheaf $A_T$ and the given complementary open and closed immersions. Its hypotheses hold because $j$ is quasi-compact; the lemma imposes no finiteness or torsion condition on the ring sheaf. It gives the actual module isomorphism $j^{-1}j_!\cong\operatorname{id}$. Applying it degreewise yields the same identity on complexes and on the ordinary unbounded derived categories. All coefficient sheaves are identified using the canonical comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image].

Write $a_\alpha:S_\alpha\to U$ for a stratum inclusion. Use its actual pro-etale inverse image, not a localization at $S_\alpha$. By composition of morphisms of sites, $(j a_\alpha)^{-1}\cong a_\alpha^{-1}j^{-1}$: the base-change site functors compose by $(V\times_T U)\times_U S_\alpha\cong V\times_T S_\alpha$. The comparison for inverse images is [lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition]; it respects the induced module actions. Inverse image on abelian sheaves is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor], and the coefficient comparisons are isomorphisms, so these module inverse images are exact and apply termwise to complexes. Applying $a_\alpha^{-1}$ to the preceding identity gives $(j a_\alpha)^{-1}j_!K\cong a_\alpha^{-1}K$. The identity and composition compatibility in [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image] identifies the coefficient actions with $A_{S_\alpha}$. Pull this isomorphism back to each of the originally given covering members, and compose it with the given perfect-model isomorphism there. The covering members and the bounded finite-projective $A$-complex $P$ are exactly the original ones; no new scalar-extension or tensor comparison is required.

source.place: Tag 03CB, lemma-composition-morphisms-sites and Definition 03CC; proetale.tex Tag 098T, lemma-morphism-big-small(2); Bhatt--Scholze Lemma 6.1.12(1)

proof.text: For the chosen closed subscheme $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$, use the identity $i^{-1}j_!=0$ of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], again with ring sheaf $A_T$. This is an identity for the actual pro-etale inverse image to $Z$, and does not require $Z$ to be an object of $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Exactness of inverse image, with the canonical coefficient isomorphism $i^{-1}A_T\cong A_Z$, allows termwise application. Every term of $i^{-1}j_!K$ is consequently zero, so the object is zero in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_Z))$.

source.place: Lemma 6.1.12(2), proved from Lemma 6.1.11; Stacks proetale.tex Tags 09AG/09AH, lemma-jshriek-zero and lemma-ses-associated-to-open

proof.text: Take $P=0$ in $D(A)$, represented by the bounded zero complex of finite projective $A$-modules. It is perfect by [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Its termwise scalar extension to $A_Z$ is the zero complex, so it is the required model on $Z$ (on the identity cover).

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11, locally constant with perfect values; the zero perfect A-complex

proof.text: The given strata remain locally closed in $T$: if their images are $F_\alpha\cap V_\alpha$ with $F_\alpha$ closed and $V_\alpha$ open in $U$, write $F_\alpha=U\cap H_\alpha$ with $H_\alpha$ closed in $T$; then $V_\alpha$ is open in $T$ and the image is $H_\alpha\cap V_\alpha$. Scheme-theoretically the closed immersion into $V_\alpha$ followed by its open immersion into $T$ is an immersion, by the definition. The chosen $Z$ is a closed stratum. Its image is disjoint from all the original strata, whose union is $U$, and their images together cover $T$. Adding this one stratum to a finite family gives precisely a stratification in [def-constructible-stratification].

split_report.summary: Extension by zero is exact on the open slice; actual pro-etale inverse images give the open identity and closed-complement vanishing for the completed coefficient ring sheaf. Compose inverse images to restrict to arbitrary locally closed strata, transport the given local models, use the zero perfect A-complex on Z, and verify the finite stratification explicitly. No new nodes.

Open restriction identity and closed vanishing for modules over an arbitrary commutative ring sheaf, applied to A_T; finite constant-coefficient recollement would not suffice.
Generic composition of actual inverse-image functors, needed for locally closed strata that need not be pro-etale site objects.
Exactness of the actual abelian inverse image, transported to modules through the canonical coefficient isomorphisms.

Generic identification of the small pro-etale site of the open U with the localized site T_proet/U; it justifies applying the ringed-site extension theorem, without replacing a compact-support argument.
